current_activity: servicing B-17s at Espiritu Santo before the landings
notes: Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 2: on 6 August 1942 General Rose, Colonel Saunders and all available hands worked a bucket line to put 25,000 gallons aboard the 11th Bombardment Group B-17s at Espiritu Santo, the group's search base for the lower Solomons. The group was already based there when the 7 August landings began. Confidence 0.5, one official family (AAF). Place is Pekoa Airfield, the wartime bomber field at Espiritu Santo.

current_activity: at Espiritu Santo; interval covers this documented operating day
notes: Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 2, covers mid-October operations; the 11th Bombardment Group continued to operate from Espiritu Santo (and to stage through Guadalcanal when it could). Recorded at Pekoa on 14 October, a documented crisis day at Henderson, because the group's interval at Espiritu covers the day. Confidence 0.5.

notes: Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 2: on 14 November 1942 fifteen B-17s from Espiritu Santo attacked the Japanese transport convoy (and earlier on the 13th–14th seventeen B-17s from Espiritu scored hits on Hiei). The group is still based at Espiritu. Confidence 0.5.

notes: On 13 January 1943 Harmon activated the Thirteenth Air Force with headquarters on Espiritu Santo (Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 3). The 11th Bombardment Group, still the South Pacific heavy-bomber force at Espiritu, is recorded on that day as coming under the new air force. Confidence 0.5.
